gaps.issue: The headline is now true and is the strongest count the evidence supports, but it does not pass the 10-second test. The README never states the question, and the H1 relies on the coined term 'next issuer value-change date'. The plain answer is that the feed posts each NAV on the next valuation morning, around 09:10 New York time. The README also gives no split by period: 7 of the 8 unseen values and 3 of the 4 late posts fall in the first six months.
gaps.fix: Rewrite the README H1 and first paragraph as a question and a plain answer, then give the precise definition. Example: 'How fast does Chainlink's Ethereum USTB feed post Superstate's daily NAV? Usually the next valuation morning, about 09:10 New York time: 588 of 601 values. 4 were a day late, 8 never posted (7 of them in 2024) and 1 is too recent to classify.' Keep 'next date the issuer's labelled NAV changed' as the stated definition of the proxy. Make the same change in the first paragraph of RESULTS.

gaps.issue: The cross-oracle comparison has only 7 values from 12 days (blocks 26,417,731 to 26,503,879), but much more history is public. The study's own router check shows the Chronicle consumer has been the router target since block 22,926,115 (July 2025). A keyless Blockscout v2 read at block 23,500,000 returned Poked events from September 2025. The bounded four-page index walk set the sample size, not data availability. RESULTS correctly says the sample supports no ranking. A full-history comparison would support one, and it is the result an RWA risk team would cite.
gaps.fix: Extend chronicle_check.py to page through the full consumer history from ROUTER_START to the pin. Pace the Blockscout v2 requests to stay under its 429 limit and keep the per-log RPC inclusion checks. Run the same next-value-change classification and unseen-value test as for Chainlink. Report both feeds side by side from July 2025 to November 24, 2026: on the next change date, late, unseen, unknown and median ET posting time. Update the chart or add a second panel only if it passes render --check.

gaps.issue: The most decision-relevant fact for an integrator is not reported: reliability changed over time. From replay delivery statuses, labels before 2025 were 118 on the next change date, 3 late and 7 unseen, out of 128. Labels from January 2025 were 470 on the next change date, 1 late, 1 unseen and 1 unknown, out of 473. Prior art (NavBridge, which ships simulated oracle data) is named only under 'Research plan leads' in SOURCES. The README never says what this study adds beyond it.
gaps.fix: Add a by-period row or table to RESULTS (Jun to Dec 2024 versus Jan 2025 to Nov 2026) computed in ustb_metrics.analyze, and test it. Add one README sentence that names NavBridge and the vendor's heartbeat parameter as the prior reference points, and states what this study adds: a measured delivery schedule on real data, a list of skipped values and an exact-match fidelity check.

gaps.issue: RESULTS says only that the cause of each of the 8 omissions is unknown. The reviewer checked all 920 stored rounds on both aggregators, including the 31 inactive ones, and none of them contains any of the 8 unseen values. That is a stronger and checkable statement: no round stored on either aggregator ever carried the values. Separately, Chronicle event completeness rests on a single third-party index (Blockscout). RPC checks confirm that each listed log was included in a block, but nothing confirms that no log was missed.
gaps.fix: Add an 'unseen values absent from all stored rounds, active and inactive' field to the replay output and state it in RESULTS next to the eight dates. For Chronicle, cross-check completeness with chunked eth_getLogs over small block ranges that a free endpoint accepts, or with a second public index, and record the result in the capture receipt.

gaps.issue: Draft 1 gives '588 of 593 matched changes' without the 8 values that never posted, so a reader takes 588/593 as the reliability rate. Its phrase 'on the next date Superstate's labelled NAV changed' is hard to parse at a glance. The standalone chart passes its automated checks: byte check, 18 words, all four mark counts. But its title 'Chainlink USTB' states no point. The lone 'Superstate' at bottom left reads as an orphan word rather than an axis label (issuer label date). 'Unseen' and 'Unknown' are hard to tell apart without the description.
gaps.fix: Rewrite draft 1 to give the whole outcome in one claim, for example: 'Chainlink's Ethereum USTB feed posted 588 of 601 Superstate NAVs the next valuation morning. 8 never appeared, 7 of them in 2024.' Change the chart title to a claim of 20 words or fewer, for example '588 of 601 USTB NAVs reached Chainlink the next valuation day'. Relabel the axis 'Superstate label date' and the categories 'Never posted' and 'Too recent'. Rerun render --check and preflight, and update the SHA-256 values in post-review.json and HANDOFF. Design approval stays with Rahil.

gaps.issue: The brief asks to compare supported pairs. The Chainlink pair is delivered in full, but the Chronicle pair covers only 12 days of its roughly 16-month public history, so that pair is effectively a sample. All other parts of the brief are delivered: the six-product availability gate closed with a narrower finding, then the USTB follow-up covered weekends, holidays, month-end, heartbeat, deviation, the chart and independent review.
gaps.fix: Same as the Chronicle full-history usefulness fix. Once it is done, the Chronicle pair counts as delivered.

gaps.issue: The tests are behavioural and cover replay tamper, live revision, switch exclusion, multicall failure, NYSE and value-change semantics, and the stale chart. Two gaps remain. Chronicle capture verification (rpc_log receipt or block mismatch, a log missing from the receipt, the page-limit overflow, unexpected router history, adapter end-state mismatch) has no test, though the Chronicle numbers depend on it. The 'after' and 'before' delivery statuses that analyze() computes are only fed to the chart test as synthetic input. No analyze() test asserts them.
gaps.fix: Add tests that patch rpc_batch and read_source to return a mismatched block hash, a receipt without the log, five full index pages and a router switch from a nonzero address, and that assert each raises ValueError with its message. Add an analyze() case where a label posts one day after its successor and assert status 'after' with days_from_next_issuer_value_change == 1.

gaps.fix: When the fixes above land, update the README and docs/README link text to 'current quality review', retitle HANDOFF for the round that implements the fixes, add the prior-art sentence and list jq as optional in 'Run it'.

gaps.issue: The digest is designed to survive issuer revisions, and a synthetic regression test covers this. The real test comes only after Superstate publishes the November 25 and later NAVs. At 05:05 UTC on November 27, official.nav_date was still 2026-11-24.
gaps.fix: After 2026-11-30, run a fresh clone: python3 scripts/feed_history.py capture, then replay > data/ustb/results.json, then python3 scripts/render_chart.py data/ustb/results.json docs/ustb-gap.svg --check. Record the result in HANDOFF. This waits only on time and does not lower the score.
